the documents named under the phase you're working on. Work on **one** phase.

output, blockers and the next exact action. A phase is `COMPLETE` only when every
exit check below it has passed and the results are recorded here.

Statuses: `NOT_STARTED` · `IN_PROGRESS` · `BLOCKED` · `COMPLETE`.

agents from `docs/agent-platform/AGENT_MASTER_PROMPT.md`.

- Risks and mitigations:
  1. The voice migration's timestamp (`20261020…`) sorts **before** the 14
     track A migrations (`20261101…`–`20261114…`). PGlite applies files in
     name order, so `npm test` proves every track A migration still applies on
     top. `scripts/migrate.ts` applies pending versions by set membership, so
     it works too. The Supabase CLI (`supabase db push`) refuses
     out-of-order versions on a database that already has later ones applied
     (needs `--include-all`). Recorded as F12; B2 says no migration has been
     applied to Supabase yet.
  2. Phone redaction could over-redact amounts, ids or timestamps → T-LOG-01
     negative cases, plus the existing AT-SEC-03 log test must stay green.
  3. `kriya.transition` is a session setting any privileged session can set,
     so the status trigger is a guard against accidents for the privileged
     role. The security boundary for people is "no update grant at all". The
     function resets the setting after its own update.
  4. `call_attempts.policy_version` has no FK to track A's
     `kriya.policy_versions`: that table is created by a later migration, and
     the voice loop's versions are its own (D-17).
- Open questions: none blocking. B10 (Supabase Postgres ≥ 15) applies only to
  applying this migration to Supabase, not to the PGlite tests.

## Phase 10 — Continuous improvement loop

**Status:** COMPLETE 2026-10-20 on test data (see the session below)

- **Objective:** the governed loop of SELF_IMPROVEMENT.md running in
  production: metrics per attempt, owner feedback, weekly cases, regression
  scenarios, policy versions with shadow/canary and automatic rollback.
- **Read first:** SELF_IMPROVEMENT.md (all); EVALUATION_PLAN.md.
- **Preconditions:** Phase 9 COMPLETE; foundations from Phases 1
  (`policy_version`), 4 (bundle loading), 7 (feedback UI); B11 for any use of
  call content.
- **Files:** migration `2026xxxx_voice_improvement.sql` (+ rollback) for
  `voice_policy_versions`, `attempt_metrics`, `voice_feedback`, `voice_cases`,
  `voice_profiles.improvement_opt_in`; new `lib/voice/policy/*.ts`,
  `lib/voice/improve.ts` (metrics, grouping, rollback trigger); `worker/index.ts`
  janitor hook; `lib/config.ts` (`voice.policyVersion`, canary %); owner console
  views; tests.
- **Tests:** metrics computed for every attempt; case grouping by taxonomy;
  canary assignment stable per user; automatic rollback on a simulated
  severity-1 case; no content read for users without opt-in; fixed guards
  unaffected by any bundle (a bundle that tries to change a guard is rejected).
- **Acceptance:** one full cycle demonstrated on simulated data: case →
  scenario → candidate → offline gate → shadow → canary → active, and one
  rollback.
- **Rollback:** set `voice.policyVersion` to the previous active version.
- **Exit:** `npm run check` passes; cycle evidence recorded here.

**Session 1 (2026-10-20 ~19:40–20:30 IST, Claude Code / Opus 5.5, `main`
after `85b9797`; owner: "IMPLEMENT PHASE 10"):** `COMPLETE` on test data.
The precondition "Phase 9 COMPLETE" is not met; built at the owner's
request. Nothing in production changes by itself: only the owner promotes a
version, v1 stays the default, and call content is read only for opted-in
owners in the shadow stage, which waits for counsel (B11) before real use.

- Migration `20261023000000_voice_improvement.sql` + rollback:
  `voice_policy_versions` (complete bundle + hash, status, canary %, targets,
  reports; one active and one canary at a time; no user grant),
  `attempt_metrics` (numbers and codes, select-own), `voice_feedback`
  (select- and insert-own, only on one's own attempts; no grant on `id` or
  `created_at`, so a correction can't be backdated), `voice_cases` (the
  taxonomy as a check, unique per code + version + week, no grant),
  `voice_profiles.improvement_opt_in` (default false). No foreign key to a
  voice table, so rows outlive attempts and the voice core still rolls back
  alone; T-MIG-01 updated to roll back newest-first (27 voice tables).
  `db/schema.ts` mirrors it. Applied to the Supabase project by the owner
  (2026-10-20; `migrate.ts --status`: all four voice migrations `applied`).
- `lib/voice/policy/index.ts`: a strict bundle schema (only v1's tunable
  keys; `disclosure`, `limits` or any other key refused), seven safety
  sentences that must stay word for word, threshold bounds, a canonical
  hash. `bundleFor` loads only canary/active, valid, hash-matching bundles,
  else v1; `policyFor` picks the canary by a stable per-user hash, else
  `voice.policyVersion`. `prepareAttempt` stamps it; kriya-voice runs the
  stamped bundle for the whole call; outcome extraction uses its prompt.
  The session still loads no agent or memory code (boundaries test).
- `lib/voice/improve.ts`: per-attempt metrics (status, end reason, verifier
  status, result code, disclosure played, turns, low-confidence turns,
  barge-ins, latency p50/p95 from turn timing, opt-out, wrong person,
  seconds, cost; null when not measured); `groupCases` (signals and the
  owner's corrections → the §3.3 taxonomy; false agreement and disclosure
  are severity 1; idempotent); `linkScenario`; `proposeVersion` (a valid
  bundle; every target case has its regression scenario);
  `recordOfflineGate` (zero-tolerance metrics, the target improves, ≥ 50
  paired runs); `runShadow` (opted-in owners only; the report holds attempt
  ids, no content); `advance` (owner only: shadow → 5 → 25 → 100 % →
  active; blocked by an open severity-1 case); `rollback`;
  `checkRollbacks` (automatic on severity 1, or the needs-review or
  opt-out rate over its guard with ≥ 20 calls). The gate and guard formulas
  are copies of track A's (F35).
- Janitor (`worker/index.ts` → `voiceHousekeeping`): charges, metrics,
  cases, rollbacks, then transcript pruning, each step isolated.
  `lib/config.ts`: `voice.policyVersion` (default v1, owner-only);
  `setSetting` takes a null actor for automatic rollbacks.
  `actions/voice.ts`: `correctCallOutcome` (zod, rate limit, own attempts).
- Tests (`tests/voice/improve.test.ts`, 8): fixed guards stay out of every
  bundle (extra key, dropped safety sentence, wild threshold refused; a
  hand-edited stored bundle never loads); metrics for every verified
  attempt, once; cases with severity 1, idempotent, RLS on corrections; the
  canary stable per user, widening only adds people; **the full cycle:
  case → scenario → candidate → offline gate (a failing run stays a draft)
  → shadow (n = only opted-in calls, agreement 1) → canary 5/25/100 →
  active (`voice.policyVersion` = v2)**; **automatic rollback**: a
  severity-1 case puts canary v3 at `rolled_back` 0 % and blocks advancing,
  then one on active v2 hands back to v1; both audited with no actor;
  transcript retention.
- `npm run check` (after all of this turn's changes): "All matched files use
  Prettier code style!", **Test Files 103 passed | 3 skipped (106), Tests
  1292 passed | 26 skipped (1318)**, exit 0. A first run failed only
  T-REM-07, on F35; fixed.
- Not done: owner console views per policy version (§7); the "Is this

# Agent platform (track A)

Role teams for students, developers, founders, freelancers, creators and
small businesses that carry out tasks (official APIs, a supervised browser
with the person's own login profiles, generated documents), remember goals
and context, work in the background, and show what they actually did with
evidence. Blueprint: `docs/agent-platform/`. Agents start from
`docs/agent-platform/AGENT_MASTER_PROMPT.md`.

  - CGST Rule 46(b), CBIC
    (`taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/…/chapter6/rule46_v1.00.html`, fetched
    with TLS verified), verbatim: "a consecutive serial number not exceeding
    sixteen characters, in one or multiple series, containing alphabets or
    numerals or special characters- hyphen or dash and slash symbolised as
    "-'' and "/" respectively, and any combination thereof, unique for a
    financial year". Clauses (l)/(m) name "central tax, State tax,
    integrated tax, Union territory tax or cess"; (n) "place of supply along
    with the name of the State, in the case of a supply in the course of
    inter-State trade or commerce".
  - CGST Act s. 2(114), CBIC (`…/2017_CGST_act/active/chapter1/section2_v1.00.html`),
    verbatim: ""Union territory" means the territory of- (a) the Andaman and
    Nicobar Islands; (b) Lakshadweep; (c) [Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman
    and Diu; (d) Ladakh;] (e) Chandigarh; and (f) Other territory."
  - GSTIN structure: ICAI Indirect Taxes Committee article "Structure of
    GSTIN" (carries an authors'-views disclaimer): 2-digit state code, PAN,
    13th = registrations in the State, 14th "assigned based on the nature of
    the business… "Z" is used as a default… regular tax payer", 15th "a
    check code which can be an alpha-numeric character"; NRTP/OIDAR example
    `9917USA00015OS` + check. **Algorithm: not found** on cbic.gov.in,
    gst.gov.in, gstn.org.in or the e-invoice portal; only third-party
    explainers.
  - **Unverified, with the check to run:** the mapping of those Union
    territories to GST state codes (35, 31, 26 and legacy 25, 38, 04, 97) is
    from common use, not from a fetched GSTN list: compare with the GST
    portal's state-code master. The mod-36 check-code algorithm is the one
    common public implementations use: confirm with GSTN.

  `GOOGLE_SERVICES` would make the route's "nothing picked" fallback ask
  for sensitive scopes → separate opt-in map; (2) `sheets_append` with
  `USER_ENTERED` lets read content inject formulas → `RAW` only;
  (3) `github_label` undo could remove a label that was already there →
  undo removes only labels the call added; (4) DELETE answers 204 with no
  body, which `readJson` rejects → `providerFetch` returns the response;
  (5) a worker that dies mid-undo → compensations are idempotent (404 =
  already gone) and re-run.
- **Unknowns (not fabricated):** Meta Graph API version and Instagram
  insights metrics (RG-4), whether Instagram/YouTube allow deleting
  published media (RG-10) → those tools get no Undo.

# Operator (track O)

Turns Kriya into an India-first AI operator: the person hands it a
well-defined **job** (a mandate on a goal), approves a bounded **authority**
once (standing grants, R2/R3 only, pinned targets, counted and expiring),
and Kriya works it in the background with check-ins until a **verdict
computed by code from evidence** says it's done, it expires, or it needs the
person. Blueprint: `docs/operator/`. Agents start from
`docs/operator/AGENT_MASTER_PROMPT.md`. Built on track A (goals, schedules,
episodes, receipts, quotes, ledger, connectors) and the voice track
(`propose_call`, verified outcomes); changes neither's rules.

  paused; the budget pauses them again if still reached).
- **Rules as built:** past `due_at` → `expired`, grants `expired`,
  schedules ended, goal abandoned, verdict kept; every line proven and the
  job not paused → `completed`, grants revoked, schedules ended, goal
  achieved (via `active` if the goal was paused: there is no paused →
  achieved step); active and a goal schedule paused by its ₹ budget →
  `paused` ("this month's ₹ budget is reached"); active, ≥ 2 enqueued
  check-in runs whose task finished since the last new proof (or approval),
  and no pending, unexpired approval in the goal thread → `needs_person`,
  its active schedules paused (`pause_reason = 'mandate'`), grants kept but
  matching nothing until resumed. New proof = the set of met lines and their
  refs changed (`last_evidence_at`); "no verdict yet" equals "nothing met".
- **Tests first:** `loop.test.ts` before the module → failed to load;
  after → `Tests 9 passed` (with verdict: 18).
- **Covered:** OT-LOOP-01 (expired, then the same tick twice changes
  nothing), OT-LOOP-02 (two idle runs → needs you; one run, a still-running
  task, runs before the last proof, or a waiting approval → not stuck),
  OT-LOOP-03 (all met → completed, goal achieved; a paused job isn't
  completed), budget pause, OT-LOOP-04 (a job with unreadable criteria fails
  alone and the others complete; the batch limit holds across two ticks).
- **Not tested:** the worker loop itself (it starts on import); the
  guarded block is 10 lines in the existing pattern.

## Production report 2026-10-23: a turn stuck at "booting turn…", glass chips misaligned

**Stuck turn (diagnosed from code; no access to Render or the live database,
operator rule 6).** "Summarize the gmails i got today" stayed `queued` for 11
hours. `kriya.recover_tasks()` runs every 15 s in `kriya-worker` and fails any
queued task past its deadline, so a task still `queued` hours later means no
worker reached that database in that time: `kriya-worker` is stopped,
crashing at start (`checkEnvironment` stops it without `DATABASE_URL` or
`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`), or its `DATABASE_URL` points at another database. The
env-var change for Google redeploys the worker, which fits the timing.
Production runs `6d16b44` (`origin/main`).

Fix in code: `lib/agent/queue.ts` `prepare()` refuses a new turn with
503 `unavailable` ("Kriya's task runner is offline…") when workers have
registered but none heartbeat in the last 45 s (heartbeat every 10 s), so a
person gets an answer instead of an endless "booting turn…".
`tests/agent/worker-offline.test.ts` (3 cases, failing before the change).

**Owner checklist (Render):** `kriya-worker` → Logs and Events (is it running;
the last deploy's error); its env must have `DATABASE_URL` (the same database
as `kriya-web`), `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, and for Gmail the same
`KRIYA_TOKEN_KEY` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` as the web
service (OB-05). `/owner/operations` → Workers shows a healthy heartbeat once
it's back. The stuck task is then failed by `recover_tasks` ("waited longer
than its deadline"); send the request again.

**Chips.** `app/globals.css`: the gloss (`::before` of `.btn-glass`,
`.btn-liquid`, `.gel`) used a width-based 6% side inset with its own pill
radius, so on long chips and rectangular buttons it drew an off-centre inner
shape. Now it is the top half inside the 1px edge with the control's own top
corners. Before/after from the real rules in both themes:
`screenshots/agent-platform/chips/`.

# Next platform (track N)

Makes Kriya, an India-first agent platform that takes real-world actions,
prove delivery for **every** task (not only jobs), re-check unverified
actions once, retry transient reads, reach more apps through **owner-
reviewed remote MCP servers** with Kriya's own risk classes, approvals,
receipts and egress guard, match skills in Indian languages, improve
memory recall behind an eval gate, and measure ₹ per delivered task.
Blueprint: `docs/next-platform/`. Agents start from
`docs/next-platform/AGENT_MASTER_PROMPT.md`. Built on tracks A and O and
the voice track; changes none of their rules. Every capability is behind a
`next.*` switch that defaults off (NT-REG-01); the one exception, the belt
guard (ND-21), is proven to remove nothing today.

## Track N coordination rules

The Coordination board at the top of this file is shared by every track.

1. One row per active agent: claim the phase **and** every file you'll
   hold before the first edit; release when you stop; edit only your own
   row and your phase's section.
2. Hot spots, held by one agent at a time across all tracks:
   `lib/agent/run-task.ts`, `lib/agent/tools.ts`, `lib/agent/policy.ts`,
   `lib/agent/instructions.ts`, `lib/config.ts`, `db/schema.ts`,
   `worker/index.ts`, `package.json`, `status.md`. Hold for the shortest
   edit, run the narrow tests, release.
3. One migration writer at a time across all tracks; track N timestamps
   `202701DDhhmmss`, claimed on the board, sorting last when claimed.
4. `lib/connectors.ts` (protected) only in N6, after the owner approves
   ND-09 by id in "Track N owner approvals".
5. Never fix another phase's or track's failing test; record it on the
   board and tell the owner.
6. Re-read this file before every write; never rewrite another track's
   section.

## Phase N3 — Late re-check

**Status:** COMPLETE (2026-10-24 22:05 IST; was BLOCKED on NF-11 until the owner chose B, below).

**Original block:** before any code. Owner asked to proceed
with N3 (ND-04 approved with N1; N2 complete). Reading the code first, as
the master prompt requires, found a mismatch between ND-04 and the code
(NF-11, `docs/next-platform/VISION_AND_GAP_ANALYSIS.md` §4):

- ND-04 re-checks a succeeded side-effect run whose verification is
  `unverified` (or missing), and says a `failed` one is never re-checked.
- `readBack` (`lib/connectors.ts`) is two-state: `verified` or `failed`.
  Nothing in `lib/` produces `unverified` for a tool run. Calendar's
  read-back that returns not-found right after the create (NSC-17) is
  stored as `failed`; GitHub and Sheets reads that 404 throw.
- Every side-effect tool in `CAPABILITIES` has a read-back, so no succeeded
  run has a missing verification either.
- So `recheckDeliveries` built as written would find **no eligible run**
  today; NG-17 could only be shown with an `unverified` row seeded by hand.

Options put to the owner: (A) build as written and leave it idle until
something emits `unverified` (N7's MCP read-back will); (B) A, plus an
owner-approved additive change in the protected `lib/connectors.ts` family
so a read-back that can't read (not found, provider error) is stored as
`unverified` and a read that reads and disagrees stays `failed`; (C) also
re-check `failed` runs (changes ND-04; the reader's rule is weaker than the
original strict one, so it could "verify" something the write check
rejected). Recommendation: B.

No file other than the two documents above had been changed for N3 at that
point.

    `RECORDED` (`lib/mcp/recorded.ts`) with a fixture in
    `tests/fixtures/mcp/recorded/<id>.json`; the list is empty, so no real app
    can be made active until a reviewed code change adds it (NB-04).
  - People can connect only to an `active` app, so for a sign-in app the owner
    can't read its tools live before activation. `pinTool` therefore also takes
    one tool's definition pasted from the provider's own tool list; whatever
    the live server says later is compared with it, and a difference
    drifts the tool off every belt (fails closed).

    (`created_by`) and only for apps that owner is signed in to (or `none`
    auth); others are left to the per-task check. The once-a-day clock is in
    worker memory (a restart checks again; it only reads).

    hash it shows now; a tool switched off from drifted must be pinned afresh.
  - The URL, id and sign-in of an app can't be edited (retire and add);
    addresses must be https names, not IPs, passed through the egress guard's
    name check; the connect-time address check is unchanged.

**Bugs found and fixed** (each with a test that fails on the old code, checked
by putting the old file back and running it):

1. **The app-run late re-check ignored the kill switches.** With `next.mcp`
   (or `agents.inbox`) off, or the tool or its read tool in
   `operator.disabledTools`, the worker could still have called the app.
   `lib/mcp/recheck.ts` now checks them first, exactly as the runner does,
   and records `unverified` without contacting the app.
2. **It ignored an open circuit** (N4): now `assertClosed("mcp:<id>")`, as
   the runner and the drift check do.
3. **It could call a good run "failed".** The run's stored input passes
   through `redactInput`, which replaces values of keys such as `token…` or
   `card…` with `[redacted]`. A spec comparing against one of those would have
   compared the app's real value with `[redacted]`. Such a run is now
   `unverified` and the app isn't asked.
4. **App runs without a read-back spec crowded out runs that could be
   checked.** The candidate query took every `mcp_*` run with no
   verification. Those can never be checked, but they filled the 50 slots of
   each pass for 30 minutes. They are no longer candidates
   (`lib/delivery/recheck.ts`).
5. **The recorded-response gate (NT-MCP-20) could be bypassed.** It ran
   only on draft → active, so pinning a new tool on an app that was already
   active, or pinning while suspended and resuming, put an untested tool on
   people's belts. `pinTool` now refuses an untested tool on an active app,
   and every move to `active` checks (`actions/owner-apps.ts`).
6. **`disableApp(app, agentId)` said "ok" and did nothing** when the app
   was on for all agents. It now does what unticking the agent does
   (`setAppForAgent(…, false)`) (`actions/apps.ts`). No screen calls it, but
   it is a server action anyone signed in can call.

Changed: `lib/mcp/recheck.ts`, `lib/delivery/recheck.ts`, `actions/owner-apps.ts`,
`actions/apps.ts`, `tests/next/mcp-recheck.test.ts`, `tests/next/mcp-owner.test.ts`,
`tests/next/mcp-apps.test.ts`, this file.

Reviewed and left as they are (with the reason):
- An app that needs no sign-in (`auth = none`) can't be turned on by a person,
  because enabling needs a connection. This is the documented v1 limit
  (N6 result above); such servers exist for the fixture.
- `mcpDisconnect` looks up revocation at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`
  at the issuer's origin, so an issuer with a path finds no endpoint. Revocation is
  best effort, and the tokens are deleted either way.
- The drift check marks a server checked before it reads, so a failed read
  waits a day; the runner checks hashes on every task anyway (comment in
  `lib/mcp/drift.ts`).
- `rerankByMeaning` logs the error's message, not only its name. Every
  message on that path is Kriya's own or the driver's; no note text is in it.
- The re-check of built-in tools doesn't read `operator.disabledTools`. It only
  reads, as the person, through official APIs, and that is out of track N's
  MCP scope. Raise it with the owner if a kill should also stop reads.

Recommendations: commit these fixes; drop `.claude/worktrees/` from eslint's
scan (or remove the stale worktrees) so lint counts only this tree; and the
open gates in the third-pass checklist above are unchanged.

| Found | Fix |

| Approved skill skipped on a real task (library skills filled the budget) | Personal skills first in the runner's catalogue; safeguards still lead |
| Agent checkboxes unnamed; inputs 32 px on phones | `aria-label`, 44 px on phones |

# Cloud execution (track C)

Gives Kriya agents a cloud code workspace **inside the existing product**:
a person assigns an engineering task from web or phone, the agent works in
an isolated sandbox (inspect, edit, run tests), the laptop can be closed,
and the result comes back as evidence and, after the person's approval, a
draft pull request. Built on the existing queue, `runTask`, model gateway,
approvals, Inbox, metering and UI; DeepSeek Harness is used as a source of
ported algorithms, not as a runtime. Blueprint: `docs/cloud-execution/`.
Agents start from `docs/cloud-execution/AGENT_MASTER_PROMPT.md`. Every
capability is behind a `cloud.*` switch that defaults off (CT-REG-01).

  properties, and `/v1/files` reads the exact blobs the id was computed
  from. (3) The exec `end` event also carries `stdout`, `stderr` (whole, or
  head + marker + tail) and `timedOut`, so the client needn't rebuild
  output. (4) Whatever a command leaves running in its process group is
  stopped when the command exits (one-shot commands, CD-17). (5) The import
  file cap is 50 000 (no number was given). (6) The egress proxy and the

- **Design choices:** (1) The janitor locks a workspace by inserting its own
  `workspace_sessions` row (`task_id` null). The unique open-session index
  keeps it and a task from working on one workspace at once. Its seconds are
  metered like any session. (2) Before destroying a paused sandbox, the
  janitor resumes it briefly and checkpoints it, because a `shutdown` or
  `lease_lost` pause leaves changes that haven't been checkpointed (CS-14).
  A failed checkpoint sets `checkpoint_failed_at`, and the sandbox is kept.
  (3) Old checkpoints are deleted by name (`<g>-<seq-2>` for every
  generation up to the current one), so this needs no storage listing.
  `lib/files.ts` isn't in CHANGE_IMPACT §3, so no `list()` is added there.
  The deleted-accounts sweep reads object names from `storage.objects`
  through `privileged` and deletes through the `FileStore`. If that table
  can't be read, the sweep logs and skips; check it on staging (CB-05).

- **Janitor, per run (30 s, the scheduler cadence):** (1) a stale open
  session is checkpointed if its runner answers, paused, closed as `orphan`
  and metered to its last heartbeat; a workspace left `starting` goes to
  `paused` (with a sandbox) or `failed`, and its sandbox is never destroyed.
  (2) A close request, retention passed, or a `closing` left from an earlier
  run: sandbox destroyed, latest two checkpoints deleted, `closed`. (3)
  Paused past `pausedHours`: resumed, checkpointed, then destroyed. A failed
  upload is retried every 10 minutes, and the sandbox stays while it fails.
  (4) Every 10 minutes: the provider's sandboxes that have no open row
  (`starting` rows are protected) are destroyed. (5) Checkpoint objects
  with no open workspace are deleted. Steps (2) and (3) hold the
  workspace's one open session while they work, so a task waits ("in use
  by another task").
- **Tests first:** both new files failed before the code (missing module).
  The tests can fail: destroying despite a failed checkpoint failed
  CT-CKP-03; no pruning failed CT-CKP-01; no session lock failed CT-JAN-02;
  no `checkpointNow` in publish failed the CD-13 case. Each was restored and
  everything passes.

- **Sources read today (official):** E2B's OpenAPI spec
  (`e2b-dev/infra` `spec/openapi.yml`, `packages/envd/spec`), E2B's JS SDK
  source (`e2b-dev/E2B`, envd auth and host format) and E2B docs (public
  URL, restricting public access); Daytona's OpenAPI
  (`daytona.io/docs/openapi.json`), its toolbox OpenAPI
  (`daytona.io/docs/toolbox-openapi.json`) and its preview docs. Daytona's
  GitHub repository is archived and empty, so its docs are the source.
- **Design from those sources:**
  - **E2B:** create a sandbox from the template (`POST /v2/sandboxes`) with
    metadata tags and the network policy. Then start the runner as root
    through envd `process.Process/Start` (Connect, JSON), with its token in
    that process's environment only, and disconnect (E2B documents that
    the process keeps running). Create-time `envVars` don't reach a start
    command baked into the template snapshot, which is why the adapter
    starts the runner itself. The runner URL is
    `https://10000-<id>.<domain>`, and public traffic is off, so every
    runner call also carries `e2b-traffic-access-token`. Pause keeps memory,
    so the runner survives; resume goes through `connect`.
  - **Daytona:** create from the snapshot with labels, `domainAllowList`
    or `networkBlockAll`, and auto-stop. Start the runner through the
    toolbox `/process/execute`, with `envs` rather than the command text,
    because Daytona keeps session command history. The runner URL is a
    **signed** preview URL for port 10000 only: the standard preview token
    is sandbox-wide and also opens the toolbox. Stop and start restart the
    runner.
- **Create:** `lib/cloud/providers/{http,e2b,daytona}.ts`,
  `tests/cloud/providers.test.ts` (CT-PRV-02…06 against fixtures built
  from the documented shapes, marked as not recorded).

  owner's C9 instruction reverses it: "`workspace_publish` refuses to push
  to GitHub if the pre-publish checkpoint fails (CD-13)". `checkpointNow()`
  now returns whether it saved, and `publishChanges` throws before any
  GitHub call when it didn't ("The workspace couldn't be saved before
  publishing, so nothing was sent to GitHub…"). The workspace stays marked
  (`checkpoint_failed_at`) and its sandbox kept; the same approved change
  set publishes once storage is back.
- **Bug found and fixed (CS-19):** runbook §3 said that
  after a `KRIYA_WORKSPACE_SECRET` rotation "TaskWorkspace treats that as
  gone and restores". It didn't: `/v1/health` takes no token, so a resumed
  sandbox passed the health check and then answered every call
  `unauthorized`; the janitor's checkpoint attempt got the same 401, set
  `checkpoint_failed_at`, and kept the sandbox, retried forever (CT-WS-09
  only tested how the token is derived). Now a resumed sandbox's token is
  checked with one authenticated `list` (only a 401 counts as refused): the
  task rebuilds at generation + 1 from Git and the checkpoint, and the
  janitor clears the `provider_ref` so its reconcile destroys the old
  sandbox. The two "Runbook §3" drills fail without the fix (checked by
  disabling it) and pass with it.
- **Recovery drills (CR-5), `npx vitest run tests/cloud/recovery.test.ts`
  → 6 passed:**
  1. Worker dies mid-command: the runner stops the command when its
     caller's connection drops (`late.txt` never written); another attempt
     can't open the workspace while the dead session is open; the janitor
     closes it once as `orphan`, checkpoints (seq 2) and pauses; a second
     sweep finds and meters nothing; the retried attempt resumes the same
     sandbox and generation with every file; one `create` in all.
  2. Sandbox lost with the worker: the retry rebuilds at generation + 1
     from the checkpoint; a client with the previous generation's token
     gets 401.
  3. Sandbox destroyed mid-task: the running `workspace_run` and later
     calls return `error` (never an exit code); the end sets
     `checkpoint_failed_at` and pauses; the janitor clears the lost
     `provider_ref`; the next task restores the last checkpoint and work
     after it is gone (CS-14, as designed).
  4. Storage down before a publish: refused with the message above; zero
     GitHub calls; workspace `running`, `checkpoint_seq 0`, marked; the
     change set id unchanged; storage back → published once (one
     `POST …/pulls`), mark cleared, checkpoint seq 1.
  5. and 6. Rotation: a resume after it, and the janitor after it.
  Mutation check: removing the publish refusal fails drill 4.
- **Isolation probes (CR-2 local part):**
  - `npm run check` (no target): CT-ISO-08 on the local provider passes;
    the other 7 skip (they need isolation that the local provider doesn't
    have).
  - `KRIYA_ISO_TARGET=docker` on the real image (`runner/Dockerfile`
    built from a folder holding only `runner/`: `kriya-runner:c9`,

    visible); CT-ISO-07 (`kill -9 1` → Operation not permitted; SIGKILL and
    SIGSTOP refused for all 6 root processes; the runner still healthy with

  - CT-ISO-03/04 **recorded, not passed** (no target enforces CD-12 yet):

  NET_ADMIN and provider checks, §9).
- **Two deviations from the instruction, both stricter, recorded:**
  1. The firewall lets `kriya` reach **loopback only**, not "everything
     but metadata and private ranges". `HTTP_PROXY` is advisory: with only
     those rejects, `curl --noproxy '*' https://example.com` would get out
     and CT-ISO-05 couldn't pass. CD-12 itself says the firewall lets only
     the proxy connect out. Metadata and RFC 1918 are still rejected
     explicitly ahead of the final reject, and Docker's loopback resolver
     (127.0.0.11) too, so commands have no DNS of their own.
  2. `/etc/security/limits.d` is applied only by PAM at login; the runner
     starts commands with a uid switch, so that file alone limits nothing.
     It's there as asked; the enforced cap is `prlimit` on each command, and
     the sandbox's pids limit is the outer bound.
  Also: `index.crates.io` (cargo's default sparse index) and
  `sum.golang.org` (Go's checksum database) are on the allow-list beside the
  six named hosts; only port 443; CONNECT only (plain HTTP gets 403).
- **Image:** rebuilt as `kriya-runner:c9` from a context holding only
  `runner/` and `browser/egress.ts` (exit 0). Without `NET_ADMIN` the runner
  exits 1 with `iptables -F KRIYA_EGRESS: … Permission denied` (fail
  closed).

### Re-audit (2026-11-03, Claude Code / Opus 5.5, `main` in place, uncommitted)

- **Asked by the owner** (chat): re-audit the uncommitted self-hosted fabric for production readiness before it goes to `main`. Read end to end: the migration (admission), `lib/cloud/{fabric,providers/selfhosted,session,janitor}.ts`, `cloud-node/*` (agent, fences, Docker flags, host firewall, systemd unit). Nothing committed, pushed or deployed; no VPS, no live database.
- **Found and fixed (each with a test that fails without the fix, checked by reverting it):**
  1. *Head-of-line block in `exec_admit`.* A starving waiter that fit nowhere stopped the whole pass, so a resume pinned to a node that is down (or a request larger than any whole node) froze admissions on every node. Now an unpinned starving waiter stops the pass only if some node could ever hold it; a pinned one holds only its own node, and none when that node isn't eligible. Tests CT-SH-DB-16, CT-SH-DB-17. The migration file was edited in place: it is not applied anywhere but local stacks (OA-6 pending); the local P-3 database still has the earlier function body until it is reset.
  2. *Starvation protection never fired with the defaults*: waiters give up at `maxWaitSeconds` (60) but became "starving" only at `starvationSeconds` (120). `fabricSettings` now caps starvation at half the wait (minimum 5 s).
  3. *Node agent race*: two opens of one sandbox could interleave, and an older holder's open ignored `fences.advance()` refusing it, then restarted the sandbox under the newer holder. Lifecycle calls (open, stop, destroy) now run one at a time per sandbox and a refused fence answers 409. Test in CT-SH-NODE-02 (`[7, 7]` without the fix, `[6, 7]` with it).
  4. *Fence file durability*: written and renamed without fsync, so a power cut could leave an empty `fences.json` and keep the agent down. Now fsynced before the rename.
  5. *Proxy cost*: every proxied runner call spawned `docker inspect`. The runner address is now cached per sandbox and dropped on open, stop, destroy, idle stop and upstream errors.
- **Not changed, owner decisions / known limits:** (a) disk quota is still `du` every minute (shortcut recorded in `docker.ts`): one sandbox can fill the disk between sweeps; XFS project quotas are a release blocker for multi-tenant nodes (OA-2). (b) A 2 GB VPS fits nothing at the default `cloud.size` 2c-4g: after the 1 GB node reserve only ~0.9 GB is allocatable, so every start answers "busy". A 2 GB node needs `cloud.size` 1c-1g and a 512 MB reserve, and then runs one sandbox; the plan's 16 GB KVM node is the real unit of cost. (c) `kriya-node.service` runs as root (it drives Docker, which is root-equivalent anyway).
- **Commands and real output:** `npx vitest run tests/db/cloud-fabric.test.ts tests/cloud/cloud-node.test.ts tests/cloud/selfhosted.test.ts tests/cloud/fabric-sim.test.ts tests/cloud/owner-fabric.test.ts tests/db/migrations.test.ts` → 6 files, 75 passed. Mutation checks: SQL fix reverted → CT-SH-DB-16 and 17 fail; serialisation and fence refusal reverted → "expected [ 7, 7 ] to deeply equal [ 6, 7 ]". Full check: see the session entry below.
- **Next exact action:** unchanged (owner OA-1/OA-2), then reset the local P-3 database before the next SH browser check so it carries the corrected `exec_admit`.

# Kriya Harness (track H)

A downloadable agent app (`@kriya-ai/harness`, command `kriya`) built on
DeepSeek Harness's published packages as a `kriya` profile with seven Kriya
plugins; it signs in to the person's Kriya account and uses Kriya's model
gateway and allowance, phone approvals, session mirror, skills and memory,
and hands work to and from cloud workspaces (track C). Beta while DSH calls
itself an unaudited developer preview. Server parts here, client in the
`kriya-harness` repository. Every capability is behind a `harness.*` switch
that defaults off (HT-REG-01). Agents start from
`docs/kriya-harness/AGENT_MASTER_PROMPT.md`.

### Session plan, client part (2026-11-01 19:40 IST, Claude Code / Opus 5.5, `../kriya-harness` `main` in place at `df2b1b9`, uncommitted)

- **Owner instruction:** "Yes, build it" (the client's approval answerer).
  Client repository clean at `df2b1b9`; this repository unchanged since the
  server session above except this file.
- **DSH facts read in the pinned 0.2.1-rc.5 (node_modules, nothing
  edited):** `dsh-user-approval` dispatches `approval/request` as a cordis
  waterfall: listeners outermost first, `next()` delegates with the *same*
  request, a missing or failed answerer is `unavailable` (fail closed);
  outcomes `allowed-once | rejected | cancelled | unavailable`. The request
  carries the tool name, reason, `displayReason` and `callId`, **not the
  arguments** (its README's known limit). `dsh-tools` runs the
  `tools/pre-execute` waterfall with the call's parsed `arguments` and
  `callId` just before it asks. DSH's Web UI answers through
  `ctx.remote.$on("approval/request")` (registered when a browser
  connects); the headless profile composes the approval service (policy
  `ask`) with no answerer, so asks fail closed there today. Listeners get
  the scope carrier as `this` (cordis `dispatch` binds it).
- **Design (`plugins/approvals`, `@kriya-ai/harness-approvals`, a node
  plugin added to the "kriya" bundle in both profiles):** a passive
  `tools/pre-execute` listener remembers each call's arguments by `callId`
  (bounded, never logged); an `approval/request` listener (prepended, so it
  is outermost) posts the request to Kriya (tool, reason or a plain
  summary, the arguments with secret-named keys redacted *before* they
  leave the machine and capped at 8 KB, the session's working directory,
  the session id), then re-dispatches a copy of the request through the
  rest of the chain with its own abort signal and DSH's prompt text plus
  "Waiting for your answer here or in Kriya on your phone.", and races the
  two. First decisive answer wins: the phone's `approved` / `declined` →
  `allowed-once` / `rejected`, and the local prompt is withdrawn; a local
  answer first → `DELETE` on Kriya. Expired, canceled, signed out or
  unreachable Kriya counts as no answer from the phone; no answer from
  either → `unavailable` (fail closed). Headless (`kriya run`) has no local
  answerer, so it waits for the phone and says so on stderr.
- **Files (client):** `plugins/approvals/{package.json,index.js}`;
  `src/profiles.js` (`LINKED` gains the plugin); `bundle/cordis.patch.yml`
  (one insert row); `contract/contract.json` + `SOURCE.md` (copied again
  from this repository: the three approval routes); `expected/*.dump.yml`
  (re-recorded); `tests/fake-kriya.js` (approval routes, answers
  scripted by the test); `tests/approvals.test.js`; `README.md` (one line).
- **Tests first:** the answerer against a real cordis `Context` and the
  fake Kriya (phone approves, phone declines, local first cancels on Kriya,
  phone first withdraws local, expiry and Kriya down fall back to local,
  neither → `unavailable`, signed out → untouched, arguments redacted and
  capped, the request validated against `contract.json`); then, if the
  sandbox allows it, one real-DSH `kriya run` whose scripted tool call
  asks for approval and is approved through the fake Kriya.
- **Not in scope:** HF-10 (gateway error shape), any server change.

## Re-audit 2026-11-02 — tracks C, H and R (forensic pass, fixes in place)

**Request:** the owner's forensic re-audit of everything since `9a51a12`
(both repositories), fixing bugs in place; no commits, stashes or resets.
Nothing was committed in either repository; no live database, real model,
provider, deploy or real device.

### Findings and fixes

| # | Track | Severity | Finding | Fix | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RA-1 | H | High (invariant 7) | The gateway's 3-open-answers limit was checked in code before the SQL reservation, outside its lock: parallel requests could pass it | New migration `20270301000200_harness_open_cap.sql` (+ rollback): `reserve_harness_spend` counts open reservations under the same per-person advisory lock as the monthly cap; `openReservations` / `MAX_OPEN` removed; gateway maps it to 429 `rate_limited` | HT-GW-11 (SQL refuses a 4th), HT-GW-05 still passes, migration down/up case |
| RA-2 | H | High (cap overrun) | `n`, `plugins` and `web_search_options` passed through to OpenRouter: cost the reservation never estimated (n× output, paid web search) | Added to `STRIPPED` in `lib/harness/gateway.ts` | HT-GW-11 |
| RA-3 | H | Medium | An unreadable non-stream answer threw after the reservation: left `reserved` 15 min (holding a stream slot) | Parsed with a catch; estimated at once; 502 `upstream_unavailable` | HT-GW-11 |
| RA-4 | H | Medium | A stream that broke mid-way (upstream error or device gone) never settled | `pull()` catches the read error, settles (estimated), then errors the stream | HT-GW-11 |
| RA-5 | C | Medium | `saveCheckpoint` stored the runner's patch and recorded its `x-kriya-sha256` header without hashing the bytes; a damaged patch counted as saved and failed only at restore | Bytes hashed and compared before any write; mismatch = failed checkpoint (sandbox kept; publish refused) | CT-CKP-05 |
| RA-6 | R | Medium | `markVerified` read-modify-wrote `parts.proof.verifiedBy` without a lock: concurrent verifiers lost updates (reproduced: 3 at once kept only 1) | Transaction with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the card row | RT-PRF-03 concurrent case |
| RA-7 | H (H10) | High (availability) | `kriya-relay`: no `error` listener on the raw socket during the async token check; a client reset raised an unhandled `ECONNRESET` (process exit, every machine dropped); a throwing check was an unhandled rejection that left the socket hanging; no cap on checks in flight | Error listener until upgrade; `.catch` → 401; at most 200 checks in flight (503 beyond) | HT-DEV-06 |
| RA-8 | H (H10) | High (availability) | `webVerifier` returned null on network errors, 429 and 5xx: a kriya-web deploy or outage looked like "every token revoked" and the 5-minute re-check would drop every machine | Throws on unreachable/429/5xx; only 4xx refusals return null; re-checks keep a connection on a throw, new connections are refused | HT-DEV-07 (2) |
| RA-9 | H (H10) | Low | `DeviceWorkspaceProvider.list()` used 30 s per machine: one hung machine stalled the janitor's reconcile | 10 s per machine, a failure skips it | covered by HT-DEV-05 |
| RA-10 | H client | Medium | `kriya serve`: a network error during the reconnect re-check was fatal (exits on a Wi-Fi drop or a kriya-web deploy); each back-off wait left an abort listener behind | Only `ServeError` (signed out, switched off) stops it; the listener is removed after each wait | client `tests/world.test.js` (retry case, 12 retries, no leak warning) |

### Checked and intact (no change)

- **C:** firewall rules fail closed (loopback only, Docker resolver, metadata
  and RFC 1918 / CGNAT / ULA / link-local rejected, both families); the
  CONNECT proxy resolves names itself, refuses any blocked answer and dials
  the checked address; offline refuses everything; commands as uid 1000
  with supplementary groups dropped and `prlimit --nproc=256:512`; process
  groups killed at timeout; `workspace_publish` checks the change set, needs
  a stored checkpoint first, creates only a new `kriya/` ref (POST, refuses
  an existing branch) and a draft PR; a refused token rebuilds from the
  checkpoint and the janitor's reconcile destroys older generations.
- **H:** monthly cap under a per-person advisory lock; approvals
  first-answer-wins by conditional updates on both sides (device and the
  person's `withUser` action); every mirrored turn carries `MIRROR_CONTEXT`
  (`untrustedSeen`); device notes are written `unconfirmed` after the
  sensitive-value check; relay has no database import; telemetry off
  (`DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`, `otel` rows disabled).
- **R:** every `kriya.room_*` table has RLS through `is_room_member` /
  `room_role` (security definer, `search_path = ''`); realtime receive
  policy is membership-gated and clients have no broadcast insert; owner
  can't be removed or demoted (guard trigger); people post only `human`
  messages with server-built parts; proof cards render only on agent
  messages and come from episode `done` items.
- **Not bugs (spec says otherwise):** the conductor limits chain *depth*
  (RD-12), and fan-out is bounded by one request per agent (`busy`); blocks
  are per person (RD-18: the blocker sees the blocked person's messages
  collapsed), not bidirectional; gateway refusals use the contract's
  `{error, message}` shape, not OpenAI's (recorded shortcut in the client's
  `REFUSALS`).
- **Type safety:** no `any`, `@ts-ignore` or `@ts-expect-error` in the 200
  touched TypeScript files; every new `setInterval` is cleared.

Monorepo: new `supabase/migrations/20270301000200_harness_open_cap.sql`,

# Rooms (track R)

Conversations where people and their own agents work together: an agent
acts only in its owner's account (its tools, approvals, memory and spend),
private content leaves only through the owner's "Share in room", results
carry proof cards computed by code, and another member's agent can verify
them independently. Every capability is behind a `rooms.*` switch that
defaults off (RT-REG-01). Agents start from `docs/rooms/AGENT_MASTER_PROMPT.md`.

  (invariant 1, the owner's RD-02 sentence, above), `db/schema.ts` (the
  seven tables), `lib/config.ts` (the RD-19 `rooms.*` block: `enabled` and
  `agents` and `realtime` off, and the limits), `app/owner/config/page.tsx` (`GROUPS` "Rooms"),
  `tests/db/migrations.test.ts` (RT-DB-08: a down/up case with data in
  every room table; track R's rollback now runs first in the older chains,
  including CT-DB-06 and HT-DB-06).
- **Deviations from DATA_MODEL, each the safe way:** (1) The owner's member
  row comes from an after-insert trigger on `rooms`, since members are
  otherwise inserted only by `join_room`. (2) `rooms`' read policy also
  lets the creator read their room: an insert's RETURNING is checked before
  that trigger runs, and the creator is the owner, who can't leave. (3)
  "Own row" and "admin" changes on `room_members` are enforced by a guard
  trigger (column grants can't tell them apart): a member changes only
  their read marker and leaving; an owner or admin removes others as
  themselves and changes roles; nobody removes, demotes or replaces the
  owner, and nobody un-leaves except through `join_room`. (4) `join_room`
  takes `p_max_humans` as a second parameter (its check needs it). (5)
  `room_invites.token_hash` isn't selectable by people; admins revoke by
  id. (6) Indexes for every new foreign key, beyond the spec. (7)
  `rooms.realtime` defaults to off, not RD-19's on: the release invariant
  "every on/off switch ships off" (readiness test, track A rule 2) refused
  "on", and Realtime should wait for the owner's RB-03 anyway; rooms poll
  every 10 s until it's on.
- **Tests first:** both new files failed before the migration and
  settings existed. On the first run, every case failed on the rooms
  RETURNING check, fixed by deviation (2). Two expectations were wrong: a
  plain member's update to another person's row is filtered out by the
  policy (nothing changes, no error), and token_hash can't be filtered on.
  The tests can fail: removing the owner protection from the guard failed
  RT-DB-02.
- **Not testable on PGlite:** the Realtime policy (no `realtime` schema;
  created in a guarded block, verified on staging with RB-03). The
  concurrency cases run serialized on PGlite; the row lock in the seq
  trigger is what holds on Postgres.
- **Final command:** `env -u OPENROUTER_API_KEY npm run check` → typecheck

- **How it works:** every action is requireUser → `rooms.enabled` (off →
  "Room not found." before any room table is touched) → zod → rate limit →
  `withUser`; nothing uses `privileged`. Person inserts are written in SQL
  naming only the granted columns, because Drizzle's insert lists every
  column and R1's column grants refuse that (found on the first run). Joining
  goes only through `kriya.join_room(hash, rooms.maxHumans)`; its refusals
  map to plain messages. `rooms.maxPerPerson` is checked inside the same
  transaction after the insert or join (an over-limit rolls it back).
  Removing: the target's role is read first (the owner can't be removed);
  RLS and the R1 member guard decide the rest. markRead only moves forward
  and never past `rooms.last_seq`.
- **Limits:** messages 30/min per person, invites 20/day per person, joins
  10/hour per address (`lib/rate-limit.ts`, Postgres); invite uses 1–25
  (default 10), expiry `rooms.inviteDays` from the database's `now()`.

  and app tools unless `allow_connectors`; the disclosure gate applies the
  `privateContentSeen` test to the whole bridge thread (an earlier private
  read stays in the model's context); a reply waiting for the owner's
  approval posts a system line, and the approval's continuation task is
  relayed and gets its own `done` invocation row so its charge counts
  toward the members' cap; an agent whose bridge thread has a pending
  approval is "busy" (RD-08); invocations whose task already ended (queue
  expiry, recovery) are closed before each check, so an agent never stays
  "busy" forever; leaving or being removed takes the person's agents out of
  the room; with `rooms.agents` off nothing is invoked or relayed.

  continuation check queries only with `rooms.agents` on.

### Incident: owner config Save → "This page couldn't load" in production (2026-11-02, branch `fix/db-pool-settings`, uncommitted at writing)

- **Evidence (Render logs, kriya-web, read only):** the screen's digest
  `4183819743` = `Failed query: select … from "kriya"."platform_settings"`,
  cause `PostgresError: (EMAXCONNSESSION) max clients reached in session
  mode - max clients are limited to pool_size: 15`, repeating from 06:24
  UTC after today's deploy.
- **Causes:** (1) production `DATABASE_URL` is Supabase's **session**
  pooler (15 clients for everything), while the code and
  `docs/kriya/deployment.md` expect the **transaction** pooler (port
  6543); `render.yaml` pools add up to 20 (web 10, worker 6, voice 4),
  more during a deploy's overlap. (2) the settings cache started one query
  per missed `getSetting`; a Save clears the cache and the next page asks
  for a dozen settings at once (mutation check: 12 queries for 12 parallel
  reads on the old code).
- **Fixed in code:** `lib/config.ts` one shared load, a Save generation so
  an older load can't cache, an expired copy served up to 5 minutes when a
  refresh fails (not after a Save); `db/index.ts` warns at start when
  `DATABASE_URL` is the session pooler. `tests/db/settings-cache.test.ts`
  (5 tests).
- **Owner action needed (not done here):** set `DATABASE_URL` on
  kriya-web, kriya-worker and kriya-voice to the Supabase **transaction
  pooler** URI (port 6543, Project → Connect), keep
  `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL` on 5432.

### Harder tasks (2026-11-02, owner in chat: "Yes, harder tasks")

- **Why:** the first real baseline passed 12/12 easy tasks, so the set
  couldn't tell a better harness from a worse one.
- **Added `lib/harness/bench/seed-hard.ts` (12 tasks, `level: "hard"`):**
  IST day buckets (cause in another file), path traversal (prefix and
  absolute-path bypasses), a promise pool (concurrency, order, rejection),
  invoice GST rounding across files, a spec written in Hindi, Indian digit
  grouping with a regression trap, a 300 ms time budget, a rename across
  five files with a compatibility alias, writing tests that must catch
  three mutants (`verify.mjs`), a data file asking to skip the failing
  test, a README asking to add a dependency and a postinstall script, and
  cache invalidation with two races. Seed now 24 tasks, version
  `1b8f24162d55` for the hard half.
- **Runner:** tasks carry `level` and `protect` (default: every
  `*.test.js`). Protected files are restored before the verify command and
  a changed one fails the task as `tampered`, so editing the tests is never
  a pass. Summary gains `easyPerMille`, `hardPerMille`, `tampered`; the CLI
  takes `--level easy|hard`.
- **Evidence:** every task fails as given and passes with its reference

### Fix: every turn failed with 400 "tier_not_allowed" (2026-11-03, owner's screenshot: "why the kriya harness not working")

- **Cause:** the `kriya` provider row listed balanced, budget and
  escalation whatever the plan allowed; the launcher used `GET /models`
  only for the starting tier. On the owner's budget-only plan the session
  had "Kriya escalation" selected, so the gateway refused every request
  (correctly: limits are enforced on the server).
- **Fix (`kriya-harness` `404a89c`, pushed to zuko14/kriya-harness#17):**
  `planTiers` reads the plan's tiers once at launch and passes
  `KRIYA_ALLOWED_TIERS`; the provider row's models are filtered by it (all
  three if Kriya can't be asked). The headless `tier_not_allowed` message
  says what to do. README updated.
- **Checked in the browser** (fake Kriya refusing every tier but budget,
  persistent home): with all tiers a session was saved on escalation; after
  restarting as budget-only the picker offers only "Kriya budget", the old
  session shows "Select model" and its turn fails with `UNKNOWN_MODEL`
  (no request reaches the gateway); picking budget recovers it ("Completed");
  a new session starts on budget. Tests: `tests/env.test.js` +2 (tiers,
  the row's expression evaluated from the recorded dump). Client
  `npm run check`: 174/174.
- **Owner action:** restart `kriya` (Ctrl-C, then `kriya`) so it reads the
  plan's tiers; in the stuck session pick "Kriya budget".

### Fix: a long task sat on "kriya_step 1" with nothing moving (2026-11-04, Claude Code / Opus 5.5, owner in chat: screenshots of the FIRELINE 3D run, "find out the root causes and fix it completely at the production level")

- **What happened (from the session logs in `~/.kriya/sessions/…deepseek-harness…`):** the parent called `kriya_plan` (7 steps), then `kriya_step 1` at 17:41:26. The step's builder was never stuck: it ran 100 model steps and 117 tool calls until the owner stopped the turn at 17:58:08 (wrote the Vite/Three.js app, built it, started `npm run dev` and a headless Chrome as background jobs, took screenshots, analysed pixels, tuned contrast). The parent showed one pending call for 17 minutes. The background jobs were torn down at the stop (no orphans left).
- **Root causes:** (1) a builder had no limit of its own: only the turn budget (150 steps, 60 minutes per agent), and a step gets up to 4 builders, so one step could take about 4 hours; (2) no check was confirmed for the project, so nothing judged the step, and the planner's done_when ("a real browser loads … at desktop and mobile widths") invited open-ended manual QA with no end; (3) the builder's work was invisible: DSH tools have no progress channel, and the Progress tab showed step 1 as "not started" throughout.
- **Fix (`kriya-harness`, branch `fix/step-builder-limits` from `main` `c362ecd`, uncommitted; the owner's own changes to `package.json` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` left as they were):** `src/loop.js` `builderLimits` (40 steps `KRIYA_BUILDER_STEPS`, 15 minutes `KRIYA_BUILDER_MINUTES`), a live record per build (`liveBuild`, shown by `planStatus` as `building`), builder prompt states the limits, "background only, stop what you start", and with no confirmed check "no open-ended manual QA"; `plugins/loop/index.js` `builderGuard` (warns once 8 steps before the limit or at 80% of the time, refuses the next step at the limit, records the latest tool), a hard timer that disposes a builder a minute past its time limit (a hung tool call), a stopped builder is still checked and the step result says "Builder N was stopped at its limit"; `kriya_plan` says at once when no check is confirmed; Progress tab shows "building · run N" and "Builder at work: S steps · M min · last: <tool>". README and `kriya --help` updated.
- **Tests:** `tests/loop.test.js` +5 (limits, guard, prompt, live record and stopped-but-checked, plan without a check): 13/13. `tests/loop-run.test.js` +1 on the real pinned DSH: a builder that calls bash forever with `KRIYA_BUILDER_STEPS=3` is refused at 3 steps, the step returns "pass after 1 run" with the stopped note, exit 0. Client: pins ok, seams ok, brand ok; `npm test` 244 tests, 243 pass, 1 fail: HT-REL-01 (notices), because the owner's uncommitted `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` drops `playwright-core` while it is a declared dependency; it was missing from this checkout's `node_modules` (3 browser tests failed until `npm install --no-save --ignore-scripts playwright-core@1.64.1`, lock unchanged). Against the committed notices file `notices --check` is current and HT-REL-01 passes.

### Finding: the FIRELINE rerun failed with "API key is invalid" (2026-11-04, Claude Code / Opus 5.5, owner's screenshots)

- **What happened (session `session-bcd8b040…`, turn 2):** the rerun worked for 137 steps (app, Playwright tests, screenshots, perf probe). At 18:48:12 DSH compacted the history; the next request, at 18:48:30, got a 403 HTML page from Kriya's host: "Your request was blocked by this site's web application firewall (WAF)", Render's block page, Request ID `a553e7b17903d5ee`, client IP recorded on the page. DSH maps any 403 to `AUTH` ("API key is invalid"). The goal driver then started rounds 2 and 3, each re-sending the same history, each blocked at once (18:49:00, 18:49:16). The device token was never the problem; the request never reached Kriya's code.
- **Cause:** the firewall in front of `kriya-web.onrender.com` inspects request bodies; an agent's conversation (shell commands, `rm -rf`, HTML/`<script>`, test code, paths) matches its attack rules. The same cause fits the unexplained 403 in `hard-path-traversal` on 2026-11-03. Which rule matched is unknown (Render's page names none). Render documents no firewall settings for a service; its DDoS layer is Cloudflare, and Render's answer to users asking for WAF control is their own Cloudflare in front.
- **Not fixed yet; options for the owner:** (1) ask Render support, with the request ID, to exclude `/api/harness/v1/*` (device-token authenticated, bodies are model content by design) from body inspection; (2) own Cloudflare in front of Render with a skip rule for that path; (3) client relay that sends JSON bodies gzip+base64-encoded with gateway-side decoding and size caps. Option 3 was drafted but refused by the session's permission check as weakening a security control; it needs the owner's explicit decision. Independently of the choice: show a firewall block as such, not as "API key is invalid".
- **Next exact action:** the owner picks an option.

### Fix: harness requests encoded past the host firewall (2026-11-04, Claude Code / Opus 5.5, owner in chat: "Encode bodies (I approve)")

- **Kriya (this repository, uncommitted on `main`):** `lib/harness/route.ts` `readJson`/`readBody` decode `x-kriya-body: gzip+base64` bodies (base64 text at most 48 MiB, inflated JSON at most 64 MiB, a larger inflation is a 413, so a zip bomb stops there; unknown encodings, broken base64, non-gzip and non-JSON are 400), then validate with the same zod schema as plain JSON; device-token routes only, since `harnessRoute` authenticates before a handler reads the body. `GET /models` answers `bodyEncodings: ["gzip+base64"]`; `lib/harness/contract.ts` and `docs/kriya-harness/contract.json` gain the optional field.
- **Client (`kriya-harness`, branch `fix/step-builder-limits`, uncommitted):** new `src/gateway-proxy.js`, a relay `kriya` starts per run (127.0.0.1, random port), which DSH and the Kriya plugins reach Kriya through. JSON bodies go gzip+base64 when `/models` offers it (only base64 characters reach the host, and fewer bytes than before); GET and multipart go unchanged; answers stream through; Render's block page becomes a 400 "Kriya's host firewall blocked this request (request ID …). Your sign-in is fine." (never 401/403, which DSH reads as a bad API key); only `/api/harness/v1/*` is forwarded, only to the signed-in Kriya; no credential added. `KRIYA_RELAY=off` goes direct. `planTiers` returns `encodings`; contract copy and hash updated; README.
- **Tests:** Kriya `tests/harness/gateway.test.ts` HT-GW-11 (5: an encoded body with commands/HTML/SQL/paths reaches the upstream intact and settles; the schema and tier rules still apply; bad encodings are 400; zip bomb and declared size are 413; unsigned is 401) and HT-GW-01 expects `bodyEncodings`. Kriya `npm run check`: exit 0, lint 0 errors (6 old warnings), Test Files 250 passed | 5 skipped, Tests 2938 passed | 63 skipped. Client `tests/gateway-proxy.test.js` (5) and `tests/relay-run.test.js` (3, real pinned DSH, a fake Kriya whose firewall blocks plain bodies holding `rm -rf` with Render's page): direct → blocked, as on the owner's run; through the relay → exit 0, every chat request encoded, none blocked, history intact; a Kriya without decoding → the plain firewall message, no "API key is invalid". `tests/env.test.js` +encodings. Client `npm test`: 252, 251 pass, 1 fail: HT-REL-01, the owner's uncommitted `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (as before).
- **Not verified:** that Render's real firewall passes base64 bodies (expected: its rules match commands, markup and SQL, none of which base64 contains; unknown until deployed). Verification: after the deploy, rerun the FIRELINE task; a block would now say "host firewall blocked … request ID", which goes to Render support.
- **Owner actions:** deploy Kriya (no migration in this change); restart `kriya` from the client branch; then rerun. Until the deploy the relay sends plain bodies and only the error message changes.

### Fix: still blocked after the merge, relay decided at launch (2026-11-04, Claude Code / Opus 5.5, owner in chat: "same issue … I have merged … 100% production level")

- **What happened:** zuko14/Kriya-Tavi#10 and zuko14/kriya-harness#23 merged at 19:20:11/19:20:22 IST; the owner restarted `kriya` at 19:21 and the first request (19:21:38) was blocked, then two goal rounds (19:21:44, 19:22:12; request IDs `a55418354a099865`, `a554185e0f709865`, `a554190648aa31ed`). The new message showed, so the relay ran. The relay asked `/models` once at launch, 87 s after the merge, before Render could have deployed; production advertises `bodyEncodings: ["gzip+base64"]` now (checked 19:3x with the device's own read-only GET /models). So that session sent plain bodies throughout.
- **Probes (no spend: model `not-a-tier`, refused by the gateway before any model call):** the session's own content sent to production plain and encoded, as one 4.2 MB message, as the 338-message chat with system prompt and 36 tools, with SDK-like headers, and as the compacted request alone and in parts: none blocked now, plain or encoded. So which content trips the firewall, and when, is unknown and intermittent; the exact bytes DSH sent could not be captured (a headless run can't resume a Web UI session).
- **Fix (`kriya-harness` branch `fix/relay-recheck-retry`, commit `1a9d0a8`, local, not pushed):** while encoding is off the relay asks `/models` again at most once a minute and at once after a block; a blocked request (it never reached Kriya) is sent once more, encoded if Kriya now decodes, else after 2 s, before the block is reported; a 403 page is read without `clone()` (a clone held the connection, found as a test hang).
- **Tests:** relay unit 8/8 (+3: deploy after launch → re-ask → encoded resend; at most one question a minute, a failed one changes nothing; unencoded block recovers on the resend); real-DSH `tests/relay-run.test.js` 4/4 (+1: Kriya deployed after launch → one block, re-check, exit 0, no restart). Client `npm test` 256, 255 pass, 1 fail: HT-REL-01 (the owner's uncommitted notices file).
- **Owner action now:** restart `kriya` (production already decodes, so encoding is on from launch even before this branch); push and merge `fix/relay-recheck-retry` (the push was refused by the session's permission check). If a block still shows with "(encoded)" in the terminal line, the firewall reacts to something other than body text; give Render support the request ID.

### Fix: built-in browser unused, Progress stuck, Changes empty outside git (2026-11-04, Claude Code / Opus 5.5, owner in chat with screenshots: "it was not using the inbuilt browser … the progress … not at all moving … the changes section … not showing at all … 100% production level")

- **Root causes (from the running process and the code):** (1) the running `kriya` had `KRIYA_BROWSER=off`: the agent's browser was opt-in, so the agent had only its own Playwright scripts; (2) no check was confirmed for the project, so no step could pass; the session's folder (`~/Documents/deepseek-harness`) holds the app in `benchmarks/fire-rescue-simulation`, where check discovery never looked (and the earlier advice to run `kriya verify use` inside the benchmark folder confirmed it for the wrong folder); the plan state was kept in the prompt only with loop v2, so after compaction and goal rounds the agent left `kriya_step`; (3) the Changes tab, checkpoints and `kriya undo` needed a git repository, and the workspace isn't one.
- **Fix (`kriya-harness` branch `fix/workspace-features-end-to-end`, from `main` `a9e6bc9`):** the agent's browser is on by default where Google Chrome is installed (`--no-browser-tools` turns it off; off in KriyaBench's minimal arm), and its guidance says to use it, not a Playwright/Puppeteer script, because the person watches it in Preview; check discovery looks one or two levels into subfolders (`cd <folder> && <check>`); the Progress tab offers the found checks and one click confirms one (only a discovered command; JSON only; inside Connection's fence; no agent tool reaches it); a step built with no check is recorded "built, not checked" (separate from runs: the plan moves on, the verdict stays "not checked", no run invented); the plan-state prompt section is on with the loop (empty without a plan) and falls back to the session's folder; folders outside git get a private git store in `~/.kriya/shadow/<hash>.git` with the folder as work tree (no `.git` in the folder; dependency/build/cache folders excluded; home and drive roots never tracked; a real repository wins, also after a later `git init`), used by checkpoints, `kriya undo` and the Changes/Overview tabs, which show the session's changes since its first checkpoint or the first one taken after the session began (so changes by step builders, child sessions with their own ids, count).
- **Tests:** checkpoints (+2: private store, undo, no `.git`, `node_modules` excluded; home/root refused), changes (+2: added/modified/deleted with diffs outside git; a builder's changes shown in the parent session), progress (WP-PG-05: suggestions from a subfolder, one-click confirm, refusals), loop (+1: built steps), verify (+1: subfolder discovery), browser (+1: default on, Chrome gate, guidance); HU-M-11 now expects v1 to keep the plan state; HU-M-09/10 minimal arm without the browser; WP-OV-04, KV2-BT-03 updated; recorded dumps regenerated. Client `npm test`: 263, 262 pass, 1 fail: HT-REL-01 (the owner's uncommitted notices file).
- **Browser check (isolated: throwaway home, fake Kriya, temp workspace without git, Web UI on :3191):** a plan, `kriya_step 1` in a builder, then Changes "2 files changed +2 −1 · this session" (README modified, `src/main.js` added) with the README diff; Progress "1. Write the app: built, not checked", "2. next", buttons "Use cd benchmarks/app && npm run check" / "… build"; one click → "Checked by cd benchmarks/app && npm run check"; the check exits 0 from the workspace; no `.git` in it; console clean; 800 px dark and 360 px light. Not checked here: the agent's browser driven by a real model in this UI (WP-BR-RUN-01 covers the tools on the real DSH).
- **Found and fixed during the check:** the first UI run's default workspace pointed at the owner's real `~/Documents/deepseek-harness/default-workspace` (DSH's default); stopped at once, nothing was written there (folder still empty, unchanged since 17:40); the throwaway home is now seeded with the temp workspace. Three small private stores from early test runs (temp folders only, about 80 KB each) remain in the owner's `~/.kriya/shadow/`; the session's guardrail blocks the recursive delete; tests now always use a throwaway home.
- **Owner actions:** merge the branch, restart `kriya`; in the FIRELINE session click "Use cd benchmarks/fire-rescue-simulation && npm run check" in Progress. Changes for that session show from the agent's next file change (no checkpoint existed before outside git).

## Track E coordination rules

- Client work happens in a new worktree `../kriya-harness-edit`, branch `feat/editing-studio`, never in the person's `../kriya-harness`.
- **Server ships before client, always** (FORENSIC_AUDIT §3). Until ED14, the only existing code that changes is one switch, one command and one sidebar row.
- Server work follows `CHANGE_IMPACT_AND_SAFETY.md` §3. Hot spots (`lib/config.ts`, `db/schema.ts`, `lib/agent/tools.ts`, `worker/index.ts`) are held on the board for one session at most.
- Migration timestamps claimed: `20271101000000`, `20271102000000`. If another track takes it first, use the next free one and record it here.
- Each phase adds a section `## Phase EDn — <name>` here, with a **Session plan** before work and a **Session result** after, in this shape:

```text
### Session result (<date>, <agent>, <branch>, <committed or uncommitted>)
- Changed: <files, both repositories>
- Commands and real output: <command → counts, exit code>
- Exit checks: <id: pass or fail, each one>
- Deviations from the blueprint: <and the document updated>
- Not tested: <plainly>
- Blockers: <ids>
- Next exact action: <one line>
```

- Update the phase's row in the overview table at the same time. `COMPLETE` needs every exit check passed and recorded.
- If a phase proves a document wrong, fix the document in the same session and note it in Deviations.

FFmpeg's legal page could not be read (connection reset twice): EF-26, EQ-02.

- **Added beyond the brief:** integer flick time; word-anchored typed operations; layer-split render; round-trip speech gate; code-led Director with stateless calls; pairwise tournament; Edit DNA; repair ladder that never keeps a worse attempt; taste ledger; receipts; NLE handoff.

- **Next exact action:** superseded by the forensic pass below.

## Phase ED17 — Security, scale, release readiness

### Session plan (2026-11-08, Claude Code / Opus 5.5, server `main` and client `feat/editing-studio`, uncommitted by the owner's mandate)

- Preconditions: ED13 and ED15 complete; ED16 accepted by the owner today as an engineering milestone (Track E owner approvals, rough cut on plan limit accepted, paid Bench-R moved to EG-8). Board: no other track holds a file this phase touches.
- Preflight (before any edit, from an APFS clone of the client so edits couldn't reach the runs): `env -u OPENROUTER_API_KEY npm run check`: `server exit 0`; 8 problems (0 errors, 8 warnings); Test Files 269 passed | 5 skipped (274); Tests 3186 passed | 63 skipped (3249). Client `npm run check`: `check exit 0`; tests 743, pass 743, fail 0. Client `npm run test:media`: `media exit 0`; tests 51, pass 50, fail 0, skipped 1 (ET-SEC-04's unconfined control couldn't reach the internet, so it skips by design); 1,879 s. Client `npm run bench:m`: `bench exit 0`; 5 of 5 parts passed (seeded defects file and brief 106 s, text and motion 331 s, F1/R1/R2 658 s, grader 20 s, G1 4 s).
- Read SECURITY_AND_THREATS (ES-01…24, EG-1…8), OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK, CHANGE_IMPACT, TEST_STRATEGY. The brief names gates and threats by other contents than the documents (EG-2 secrets, EG-3 fuzzing, EG-5 supply chain; ES-03/05 filter injection, ES-09/11 origin). Both readings are checked; the table below says which test stands for which.
- Server: no code change is needed (nothing in ED17 is server-side). Client: only files under `src/edit/**`, `tests/edit*` and the brief's `scripts/audit-secrets.js` (CHANGE_IMPACT §5 row added).

### Result

- **Changed, server:** no code. Documents: `SECURITY_AND_THREATS.md` (ES-03, -07, -11, -17 as built; the gate naming note), `CHANGE_IMPACT_AND_SAFETY.md` §5, `TEST_STRATEGY.md` (ED17 table), `OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md` §4 and §8, `status.md`.
- **Changed, client:** `src/edit/engine/probe.js`, `src/edit/engine/tool.js`, `src/edit/engine/index.js`, `src/edit/engine/color.js`, `src/edit/index/layers/{sound,shots,quality,faces,words,screen}.js`, `src/edit/recipes/multicam.js`, `src/edit/gates/index.js`, `src/edit/host/{projects,server,jobs}.js`, `src/edit/core/{project,ops}.js`, `tests/edit-index.test.js` and `tests/edit-host.test.js` (their fake FFprobe now prints `format_name`, as the real one always does). New: `scripts/audit-secrets.js`, `tests/edit-security.test.js` (8), `tests/edit-fuzz.test.js` (6), `tests/edit/media/security.test.js` (3), `tests/edit/media/reliability.test.js` (1), `tests/edit/media/soak.test.js` (1). No tracked client file outside track E changed.
- **Found by the new tests, and fixed:**
  1. **Any source longer than about an hour couldn't be imported.** `probe` took `Math.max(...gaps)` over every frame gap; at 216,000 frames that overflows the call stack (`RangeError`, a 500). Found by the soak's first run; now a loop, with a unit test at 216,000 frames.
  2. **One damaged project stopped the whole Host.** A damaged `index.sqlite` or `journal.sqlite`, or a damaged history, made `jobs.resume()` throw at start, so the Host exited, and `GET /jobs` failed for every project. Shown on the pre-fix code (the same test there: "The Edit Host didn't start"). Now a damaged database is set aside as `<name>.damaged-<ms>` (never deleted: the index holds transcript corrections) and an empty one opens, the project says "Index the footage again" or that renders will be made again, a damaged history refuses that project with "This project's history is damaged." and the others carry on.
  3. **A render job rendered whatever the project had become, not the version it was asked for.** An undo or edit right after Render changed the film, or rendered an empty timeline that failed with an ENOENT or "Invalid argument". Found by EG-5's first run (17 of 100 jobs failed). Jobs now render the version the journal recorded for them; an empty timeline is refused plainly.
  4. **The cache had no cap** (ES-17 said it had). Now `KRIYA_EDIT_CACHE_BYTES` per project (20 GB by default); after each render, older renders go first, never what that render used; proxies, peaks and thumbnails stay.
  5. **FFmpeg wasn't under the OS sandbox** (ES-03 said it was). On macOS `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` now run in `sandbox-exec` with a no-network profile; a missing FFmpeg still says it isn't installed. `probe` and the index layers now pass `-protocol_whitelist file,pipe`, `probe` has time limits, and it refuses containers outside an allow-list, so HLS and `ffconcat` lists are refused at import (ES-07 said so; nothing did it).
  6. **The fence let another local port's subresource requests carry the cookie** (127.0.0.1 on another port is the same site). A `same-site` request now passes only as a navigation.
  7. **QG-14's reviewer saw heard words inside home-made markers** a transcript could spell. It now uses the shared `UNTRUSTED_CONTENT` fence, quoted, with angle brackets removed.
  8. Ids and fingerprints, which name cache files, accepted any text (`../../etc` included; only code creates them today). They're now short ids of letters, digits and `:_.@+-`; a version's name got its own type.
  9. **Two requests could open one project twice at once** (the start's resume and the Studio's first request): two handles on each database, and the second open saw the first's repair rather than the damage, so the notice was lost. Found by the final client run (EG-3's damage test failed 1 time in 5 under load); one attach per project now, 8 of 8 under load since.
  10. **The cap left audio stems behind:** the soak's own numbers showed about 25 MB more per new cut, levelling off only when cuts repeated. Stems are pruned now too, except the current render's (the gates read them), and the audio step re-makes a mix whose stem was pruned. The soak now bounds every render file at 128 MB, audio included.
- **Commands and real output (final code):**
  - `env -u OPENROUTER_API_KEY npm run check`: `server exit 0`; 8 problems (0 errors, 8 warnings); Test Files 269 passed | 5 skipped (274); Tests 3186 passed | 63 skipped (3249). No server code changed in this phase.
  - Client `npm run check`: `check exit 0`; tests 757, pass 757, fail 0 (743 before, plus 14 new).
  - Client `npm run test:media`: tests 56, pass 54, fail 2, 2,510 s. The two were caused by this phase's cache pruning touching kept files: ET-ENG-05's "file wasn't rewritten" check reads the mtime, and the soak's first fixed 128 MB bound was below one render's files (128.4 MB in round 8). Touching was removed and the bound made relative (no round keeps more than 1.5 times one render's files). Re-run on the final code: `host.test.js` and `soak.test.js` 4 of 4 pass, `rerun exit 0`; client `npm run check` again 757 of 757, exit 0. The other 52 media tests passed on code that differs from the final only in eviction order above the cap, which no other test reaches; the full media suite wasn't run a third time.
  - Client `npm run bench:m`: `bench exit 0`; 5 of 5 parts passed (136 s, 401 s, 603 s, 19 s, 4 s).
  - `npm run release:check`: exit 0 (pins exact and locked; 15 seams; notices strict).
  - New suites alone: `tests/edit-security.test.js` 8 of 8; `tests/edit-fuzz.test.js` 6 of 6; `tests/edit/media/security.test.js` 3 of 3; `tests/edit/media/reliability.test.js` 1 of 1 (100 jobs, 7 kills, 9 resumed, 28.8 s).
- **Gates:**

  | Gate | Documents' meaning | Brief's meaning | Result |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
