Keyboard path (1/2/3 modes, transport, the focusable clip list, words as buttons); every visible target 44 px or more in every mode, words excepted as inline text targets (WCAG 2.5.8); Review mode at 360 px has no timeline and no sideways scroll; light and dark palettes match the harness's (test-checked); the console is clean. Switching Direct, Edit, Finish keeps the same monitor element and playhead; the mode is remembered per person.
  - ET-SEC-09: **pass**. The Studio's own files are refused on a foreign Host (DNS rebinding), a foreign Origin and `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`, and carry COOP and COEP (the page is `crossOriginIsolated` in Chrome); the API still needs the session; a launch link can only be minted on the owner-only socket; a `back` that isn't a loopback `http` origin on another port (another host, https, `javascript:`, credentials, the Host's own port) is dropped. ED4's ET-SEC-09 test still passes.
  - ET-REG-02: **pass**. The three dumps differ from `HEAD` only by the `kriya-edit` row; the row's condition, evaluated, is off when `KRIYA_EDIT` is unset, `off` or `false` and outside the Web UI profile; with the switch off the launch route answers 404 and loads nothing from `src/edit`.
  - Browser check (operator rule 7): **pass**, against the fake Kriya. `screenshots/kriya-editing/ED6/`: the harness row at 1280 and 360, the Studio home, Direct, Edit and Finish at 1280, Review mode Direct and Finish at 360, each light and dark; console clean in both runs. Neighbours unchanged: the other sidebar rows and the dumps' other rows are as before.
- **Found by running it:**
  - The monitor's seek read its own promise before the promise existed whenever the frame was already decoded (a temporal-dead-zone error). Latest-wins is now a counter, and `monitor.settled` lets a caller wait for the frame on screen.
  - The Studio had no favicon, so every load logged a 404; it has an inline icon now (the CSP already allows `data:` images).
  - `kriya login` against a fake Kriya in the same process hangs under `spawnSync`; the test signs in with an async spawn.
- **Deviations (documents updated where they describe the build):**
  - The monitor is STUDIO_APP §4's fallback path only: `<video>` plus Canvas 2D, two elements per asset for seamless cuts. WebCodecs, the WebGPU compositor, LUT and matte preview, the watchdog, the AudioWorklet mix and meter, workers and OffscreenCanvas, the Service Worker and the app manifest aren't built.
  - Plain DOM, no framework: the Studio needs nothing else at this size, and esbuild is the only new package.
  - Scopes are on the CPU (histogram and luma waveform); no vectorscope or false colour.
  - The timeline fits the whole cut to its width, with no zoom, and draws on the main thread (a `shortcut:` comment in `timeline.js`).
  - The harness row's page goes to the Studio at once, except when the tab just came back from it, so Back can't loop.
  - The prompt box is present, as the brief asked, and says plainly that asking for a change isn't available yet. UX_SPEC §9 says "No dead controls"; the Director (ED7) replaces it.
  - The Home screen creates a project from a typed folder path. The folder browser, drop-to-upload and the first-run Setup screen aren't built in the UI (the Host routes exist).
- **Limits and what wasn't tested:**
  - All footage is synthetic (barcodes, tones); the transcript comes from a script standing in for the speech model (EB-11). No real camera file, VFR, HDR or long edit was played. One Mac, headless Chrome only; no Safari, Firefox, Windows or Linux.
  - Playing across a cut was watched only through the frame checks and a forward and backward playback check, not judged for a visible stall. Reverse play has no sound. Speed changes and holds are in the mapping and its unit tests, but no edit with them was played.
  - `studio/dist/` is a build output in the worktree; whoever commits decides whether it's committed or built in release.
- **Blockers:** none for ED7. EB-09 and EB-11 still gate a real device and real transcripts.
- **Owner's decision (2026-11-07):** "Yes, move to ED7": ED6 stays COMPLETE, and the rest of ET-UI-02 (prompt with a selection, Proposal mode, Variations wall, drawing on the frame) and of ET-UI-03 (WebGPU compositor with one GPU device across 1,000 clip switches, the watchdog) are ED7's exit checks now (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN §1).
- **Next exact action (owner):** assign ED7. Nothing is committed, as instructed.

- **Found by running it:**
  - **ED4 bug, fixed:** the Host's idle check counted only when a request *started*, so a request still running past the idle limit could have the Host shut down under it. Opening `index.sqlite` made `POST /projects` slow enough to show it (ET-HOST-06 flaky). In-flight requests now count as activity (`main.js`, `server.js`).
  - Fillers broke trigram similarity between two attempts at the same line (recall 0.50). Attempts are now compared, and judged complete, on their non-filler words.
  - The global-shift search mistook objects moving in a still frame for camera motion, and a chart with no vertical detail for vertical shake. A shift now counts only if it beats no shift by 30%, and near-ties go to the smallest shift.
  - `swift faces.swift` took 91 s to interpret on this Mac; compiled once with `swiftc` (2 s), a run takes 0.4 s. The helper is built once into `~/.kriya/edit/bin/`, named by its source hash.

  - L8 uses Apple's Vision through a compiled helper instead of MediaPipe or YuNet: no download, nothing leaves the machine, macOS only. Other systems report the layer unavailable (PERCEPTION §2).
  - L7 is computed in code from small grey frames instead of OpenCV. Its blur and shake scales are uncalibrated, and marked so in code and in `data.calibrated: false`.
  - No `views` table: views are built by code on request (PERCEPTION §7). The brief's `retakes` table is DATA_MODEL's `sentences` plus `takes`.
  - Indexing is started explicitly (`POST /projects/{id}/index`), not on every asset add, so ED4's flows and job lists are unchanged. The Studio (ED6) starts it on drop.
- **Limits and what wasn't tested:**
  - **No real speech recognition ran.** The runtime manifest `2026.11.0` ships mlx-whisper but no model weights, L2 runs offline (`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`), and no runtime is installed here (EB-09). The Host test puts a script where the runtime's Python would be: real FFmpeg extraction, process and parsing; scripted words. The mlx and faster-whisper calls in `words.js` have never run. New blocker EB-11.
  - All media is synthetic. No real face was detected (none to detect); Vision boxes are mapped by a unit test from a scripted helper line. Thresholds (silence −40 dB, `scdet` 10, sentence gap 700 ms, filler pause 150 ms, Jaccard 0.65) are starting points, not tuned (EX-11 says tune on real labelled clips).
  - L5 has no hidden-stumble or noise check (needs pitch, L3, L4), no filler-aggressiveness setting, no speakers. L6 finds hard cuts only. L8 has no eye or chin lines or gaze. No zero crossings for the solver yet (ED9). The language defaults to the brief's, else `en`; the "ask once per project" prompt is ED6.
  - Re-transcribing an asset (a new language or model) renumbers its words; `alignWords` and `remapAnchors` from ED3 aren't wired to that yet, so an existing anchor could then point at a different word. Today nothing re-transcribes on its own.
  - Words don't stream in chunks, the viewed clip doesn't jump the queue, and FFmpeg isn't run inside the OS sandbox yet (ES-03). No Windows or Linux.
- **Blockers:** EB-11 (new): speech model weights as a signed runtime artifact, for L2 on a real machine. EB-09 still gates real devices. None for ED6.

  - `DATA_MODEL` §2 gives clips no home: `Sequence` gained `clips[]`.
  - `Clip`: `source` may be null (generated clips), `at` may be null (base clips lay end to end in list order), plus `until`, `duration`, `peak`, `loop`, `audioLead`, `audioLag`.
  - `Effect` gained `freeze`, which the `freeze` operation needs. A `Block`'s time lives on its clip.
  - `Project` gained `nextId`, so a removed id is never reissued. A word anchor gained `exact`, so a split takes no pad.
  - `apply(project, ops, ctx)`: the third argument carries the index, because anchors can't be validated without it. With no index, a word anchor is refused.
  - `punch_in` is a generated clip with a `zoom` effect on the overlay track, not an effect on a clip, so it follows its word through a re-cut and its loss is reported.
